Collection of qualitative data will additionally play a pivotal role for this 
investigation. Interviews will be conducted with different educators, parents, and 
students weekly, helping the developer uncover information regarding the 
applications usability, educational impact, and motivational elements. Critically 
interviews will to be made with individuals that have dropped-out, helping find 
fatal issues within the application that must be addressed immediately. Surveys 
maybe released periodically to reach a wider audience of stakeholders. These 
surveys will focus on user’s opinions regarding the applications user interface 
and experience, while also shining light on the content delivery system. 
The stakeholders related to this project include educators, parents, and 
students. With the primary focus being on students, they will offer critical 
feedback via their direct interactions with the application; educators offer their 
valuable experience and professional insights into how effectively the application 
integrates into the curriculum. Parents provide a unique viewpoint and will be 
able to comment on their childs engagement and performance outside of the 
classroom. 
The expected outcomes from this future investigation will involve reports 
delineating the effectiveness of individual and combinations of features. The 
findings uncovered from this study will aim to validate the initial hypotheses 
regarding the applications benefits and will help guide refinement and 
development of future applications. 
To aid this investigation a range of tools will be required. For data analysis 
software such as Microsoft Excel and Python ML libraries maybe utilised; while 
data collection could be achieved using services such as SurveyMonkey and 
Zoom. Finally statistical analysis software will be critical for evaluating the 
results from the A/B testing and the longitudinal study.
